# Issue #40 v5 Pre-Implementation Correctness Review

- Worktree: `/Users/ylpromax5/Workspace/feishuspeech/.kw/worktrees/issue-40`
- Baseline: `b321ac5d6c04c91ced9afeb2240f9566d9b8d305`
- Candidate: `/Users/ylpromax5/Workspace/feishuspeech/kaola-workflow/issue-40/architecture-blueprint-v5.md`
- Runtime evidence: `/Users/ylpromax5/Workspace/feishuspeech/kaola-workflow/issue-40/.cache/runtime-diagnosis-v5.md`
- Scope: pre-implementation correctness and feasibility of the v5 architecture, state/authority, AppKit focus and key routing, target binding, deadline/executor/lock composition, one-shot lifecycle, recovery/refocus, executable TDD plan, file ownership, and dependency order

## Verdict

FAIL. The authority, fixed-target, nonactivating-panel, and one-shot post-boundary direction is substantially sound, but three implementation-blocking architecture defects remain: the absolute deadline is not carried into or enforced by the final gate and does not cover every AX object; the proposed native default Send action contradicts the Control+Return pass-through rule; and the mandatory baseline deadlock RED has no safe executable route under the stated test-only custody and build order.

## R1 - The 2-second whole pre-boundary deadline is absent from the operations that can block

- Failure class: unbounded pre-boundary wait / UI lifecycle liveness contract gap.
- Trigger: either (a) an exact-cursor attempt reaches a slow system-wide focused-element AX query, (b) a submission job waits behind a delayed job on the dedicated serial executor, or (c) the interference epoch lock is unavailable until after the permit's remaining budget. No Unicode key-down has yet been attempted.
- Expected: the one absolute deadline that begins when the permit is consumed must terminate every such case by two seconds as `notStarted(.deadline)`, preserve the exact draft, restore editable preview focus, and keep the MainActor heartbeat live (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:363-394`).
- Observed: `ReviewUnicodeCommitter.commit` accepts only the prepared pair and expected epoch, not the absolute deadline (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:325-332`). Its required algorithm says to enter the nonrecursive critical section, compare only the raw epoch, and post down when equal; it specifies neither deadline-aware lock admission nor a deadline recheck inside the lock immediately before down (`:334-344`). A dedicated serial executor moves an unbounded wait off MainActor but does not make it bounded, and Swift task cancellation cannot preempt a synchronous lock acquisition or AX call.
- AX proof: the blueprint budgets a 500 ms timeout only as a per-element exact-cursor operation (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:366-374`). The current exact restore path then calls `runtime.focusedElement()` after setting the captured element (`FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:245-275`), and production `focusedElement()` creates a different system-wide element and performs `AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue` on it (`:399-408`). The local SDK explicitly says a timeout set on one accessibility object applies only to that object and not even to other equal objects; the system-wide object must be configured separately if it is used (`ApplicationServices.framework/Frameworks/HIServices.framework/Headers/AXUIElement.h:387-402`). Therefore the proposed per-element timeout does not bound this existing pre-boundary call.
- Executor/isolation proof: the project uses `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor` for app and tests (`FeishuSpeech.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:401-405`, `:427-430`), and the current delivery, accessibility, event backend, event handles, and monitor interfaces are explicitly MainActor-isolated (`FeishuSpeech/Services/ReviewDestinationDelivery.swift:20-60`; `FeishuSpeech/Services/AccessibilityClient.swift:12-84`; `FeishuSpeech/Services/TextInputSimulator.swift:519-567`, `:1016-1175`; `FeishuSpeech/Services/CurrentFocusAppendSession.swift:136-152`, `:722-773`). The blueprint requires an off-MainActor executor but supplies no isolation/Sendable ownership split for moving `AXUIElement` and prepared `CGEvent` capabilities to it (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:379-390`). Without that explicit split, a superficially queued implementation can still hop back to MainActor and reproduce the failed heartbeat.
- Reproducible scenario: hold or delay the real epoch gate beyond the deadline, or inject an exact-route AX runtime whose system-wide focused-element query returns after more than two seconds. The specified committer has no deadline value with which to reject after gate acquisition, and the specified AX timeout does not cover the system-wide element. The attempt can remain preparing after the promised bound; if the current MainActor-isolated stack is retained, the heartbeat also stops. The installed sample already proves that a synchronous pre-boundary lock wait can persist through all 2,620 observations (`runtime-diagnosis-v5.md:40-57`, `:63-87`).
- Why existing guards do not prevent it: a raw epoch equality check proves interference state, not time. An absolute deadline held only by the coordinator cannot stop synchronous worker code after dispatch. A target-element AX timeout does not apply to the separately created system-wide element. One active permit prevents duplicate attempts but does not make the active attempt return.
- Minimal repair boundary: add the same absolute monotonic deadline to executor admission, every AX operation, event preparation, and `commit`; use deadline-aware gate acquisition and recheck both deadline and raw epoch while the gate is owned immediately before down. Explicitly define a nonisolated/Sendable submission worker that owns the serial executor, epoch commit primitive, prepared CGEvent pair, and system AX runtime, while MainActor passes only immutable identity/draft/deadline snapshots and applies typed receipts. Configure a bounded timeout on every AX object actually messaged, including the system-wide/application object used for focus verification, or replace that query with a bounded target-application query. Add tests for executor queue delay, a lock held past deadline, a system-wide AX delay, and MainActor heartbeat in the concrete production composition.

## R2 - A native default Send button turns Control+Return into confirmation

- Failure class: keyboard-routing authority bypass / unintended explicit output intent.
- Trigger: the editable preview panel is key, the native editor is first responder, and the user presses Control+Return or Control+keypad Enter.
- Expected: Option/Control Return must pass through to the editor and must not create `ReviewConfirmationIntent`; only unmodified plain Return/keypad Enter, optional retained Command+Return, or a real Send click may confirm (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:409-420`).
- Observed: the design also requires the Send control to become a native default action so that plain Return can activate it when another preview control is first responder (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:411-424`). AppKit's default-button contract says the window receives Return/Enter when no responder claims it and also when Control is pressed with Return. AppKit sends Control-key events through `performKeyEquivalent` before the first responder's `keyDown`; an `NSButton` Return key equivalent acts as a click. See [Apple NSWindow defaultButtonCell](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindow/defaultbuttoncell) and [Apple Cocoa Event Handling Guide, Handling Key Equivalents](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/Cocoa/Conceptual/EventOverview/HandlingKeyEvents/HandlingKeyEvents.html). The local SDK exposes this default-button mechanism at `AppKit.framework/Headers/NSWindow.h:671`.
- Concrete baseline path: the current editor deliberately passes Option/Control Return to `super.keyDown` and only constructs `.qualifiedReturn` for accepted modifiers (`FeishuSpeech/Views/TranscriptionReviewView.swift:361-385`). Under the proposed default action, Control+Return is offered to the window/button key-equivalent path before that editor guard. The visible Send callback can then construct `.sendButton`, so the coordinator cannot distinguish the excluded keyboard gesture from a real click.
- Reproducible scenario: make the real panel key and the real editor first responder, install the proposed native default Send action, dispatch a native Control+Return event through `NSApplication.sendEvent`, and count the opaque intents. AppKit routes the default-button action and yields one Send intent where the blueprint requires zero. Existing state/permit guards validate authority and exactly-once, but they do not validate whether the button action arose from a mouse click or this excluded default key equivalent.
- Why existing guards do not prevent it: `ReviewConfirmationIntent` proves only that a UI gesture site constructed it. Once the default button treats Control+Return as its action, the button site is itself the confused deputy. The editor's `hasMarkedText` and modifier checks are too late when the event is claimed as a key equivalent.
- Minimal repair boundary: define one concrete preview-local Return arbiter instead of relying on an unrestricted native default action. It must verify the exact key panel, first responder, repeat state, modifiers, and marked-text state before routing: the editor keeps plain/Shift/IME/Option/Control handling when it is first responder; a fallback Send action may accept only unmodified, nonrepeating Return/Enter when another preview control is first responder. Prevent the default button from claiming Control/Option/Shift/marked-text events. The native-event tests must separately cover Control+Return and Control+keypad Enter through the full panel/application route and assert zero intent and zero delivery.

## R3 - The required production-composition RED cannot be run safely in the declared TDD lane

- Failure class: non-executable regression oracle / ownership and dependency-order gap.
- Trigger: build-order step 1 asks the TDD role to land and run the concrete production-lock deadlock RED against `b321ac5` before any shared-type or production repair (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:583-589`). The test invokes the current production epoch, monitor, and review delivery composition that is known to acquire the same nonrecursive lock twice.
- Expected: the parent test must be able to terminate a child that deadlocks and report a bounded RED without hanging the hosted XCTest process; after repair, the same production composition must return normally (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:502-520`).
- Observed: the blueprint offers either a subprocess/helper or a reentrancy-detecting production seam (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:512-520`), but neither exists or has an owner in step 1. The project currently has only the FeishuSpeech application and one hosted unit-test bundle; `FeishuSpeechTests` uses `BUNDLE_LOADER`/`TEST_HOST` and there is no helper executable target (`FeishuSpeech.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:88-134`, `:409-456`). The TDD lane is restricted to seven test Swift files and explicitly denies implementers test edits (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:431-444`); it is not assigned `project.pbxproj`, a helper source/target, or the production epoch file. The alternative reentrancy seam necessarily changes the production lock in `CurrentFocusAppendSession.swift`, which belongs to the later output implementer (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:446-454`) and therefore cannot exist for the baseline test-only RED.
- Reproducible scenario: implement `test_productionCommitGateNeverReentersNonrecursiveEpochLock` in the hosted test target by calling the concrete baseline composition. Running it in-process wedges the thread at the nested `NSLock`; cancelling a Swift child task cannot interrupt that lock and may hang the test host. Spawning the test-hosted bundle directly is not a defined helper protocol, and adding the missing helper target violates the current file ownership/order. The runtime diagnosis confirms that all current delivery tests avoid this composition and explains why the green suite missed it (`runtime-diagnosis-v5.md:126-150`).
- Why existing guards do not prevent it: XCTest expectations and task timeouts are cooperative; they cannot kill a thread blocked in `NSLock`. A fake lock or unlocked monitor violates the blueprint's own production-composition requirement. The final installed UAT occurs too late to replace a deterministic regression oracle.
- Minimal repair boundary: before TDD step 1, choose and specify one executable isolation mechanism. Either add a dedicated helper executable/test target with its source, `project.pbxproj`, invocation protocol, timeout/termination cleanup, and explicit TDD ownership, or authorize a narrowly scoped production reentrancy detector/diagnostic entrypoint as a prerequisite architecture step and assign its production owner before the RED lane. The oracle must first prove the baseline deadlock in a killable child, then exercise the repaired concrete epoch + monitor + committer composition, not merely a fake or a non-reentrant no-op closure.

## Surfaces that are otherwise coherent

- The draft authority, opaque UI intent, one-shot permit, prepared-pair provenance, and phase-aware receipt separate recognition/barrier authority from UI and output capability (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:184-269`). Ordinary `.editable` remains action-2-plus-recorder-barrier-only.
- The nonactivating panel topology correctly separates target frontmost identity, preview key/editor receiver, and FeishuSpeech activation, with installed WindowServer behavior retained as a UAT gate (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:65-140`).
- Target capture remains immutable and fixed to PID, bundle ID, executable URL, and launch date; both exact and application-bound delivery fail closed on identity/frontmost/security drift and never ambiently retarget (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:142-182`).
- The state machine consumes one permit, preserves exact drafts on pre-boundary failure, and makes every key-down-attempt outcome terminal submitted-unverified with no ordinary retry authority (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:271-305`, `:396-405`).
- The file lanes are disjoint for ordinary output versus UI work after shared types are defined, and the protected recording/recognition topology remains explicitly unchanged (`architecture-blueprint-v5.md:429-485`, `:641-657`). R3 is the specific missing helper/project ownership exception.

## Validation disposition

This is a read-only architecture review. No production or test file was edited and no test suite was run after the three admitted defects made the candidate non-passable. The reviewed worktree was clean at `b321ac5d6c04c91ced9afeb2240f9566d9b8d305`.
